evidence.claim: The Egyptian president is the head of state and head of executive power under article 139 of the constitution.
evidence.title: President of the Republic
evidence.excerpt: The Egyptian president is the head of state and head of executive power under article 139 of the constitution.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official constitutional summary from the Egyptian state information service; the office definition is stable across 2022.
evidence.period_fit: Stable constitutional authority in force during 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Defines Abdel Fattah el-Sisi’s office, but not any specific 2022 action.
contrary_evidence: Constitutional authority alone does not show direct control over every security or nuclear decision.

evidence.claim: The IMF said the EFF would support macroeconomic stability, debt sustainability, exchange-rate flexibility, lower inflation, stronger social protection, and reforms to reduce the state footprint, enhance transparency, and promote private-sector-led growth.
evidence.title: Egypt: IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement on an Extended Fund Facility Arrangement
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said the EFF would support macroeconomic stability, debt sustainability, exchange-rate flexibility, lower inflation, stronger social protection, and reforms to reduce the state footprint, enhance transparency, and promote private-sector-led growth.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct IMF statement on the policy package negotiated with Egyptian authorities.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Sisi's government and its economic program.
contrary_evidence: It is an IMF-stated program design, not proof that reforms were fully implemented in 2022.
The same package was driven by crisis pressure as much as by pro-growth intent.

evidence.claim: World Bank data for 2022 show adult unemployment at 5.5 percent, adult inactivity at 50.1 percent, female inactivity at 82.5 percent, and undernourishment at 7.9 percent, indicating weak labor-market inclusion and household vulnerability.
evidence.title: Economy | Egypt, Arab Rep. | World Bank Human Capital
evidence.excerpt: World Bank data for 2022 show adult unemployment at 5.5 percent, adult inactivity at 50.1 percent, female inactivity at 82.5 percent, and undernourishment at 7.9 percent, indicating weak labor-market inclusion and household vulnerability.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank data portal with 2022 indicators, though presented as a dashboard rather than a narrative report.
evidence.ruler_attribution: These are household and labor-market outcomes under Sisi's tenure; they reflect broad conditions more than a single policy choice.
contrary_evidence: The dashboard is descriptive, not causal.
Labor-market outcomes are shaped by long-run structure and external shocks as well as government policy.

evidence.claim: The 21/2022 social welfare plan said social protection would expand to poor and vulnerable groups, with EGP 283.4 billion allocated to social protection and targets including 4 million poor families, 18 million insured workers, and higher pensions.
evidence.title: Egypt’s Ministry of Planning and Economic Development announces pillars of 21/2022 social welfare plan
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Planning and Economic Development
evidence.excerpt: The 21/2022 social welfare plan said social protection would expand to poor and vulnerable groups, with EGP 283.4 billion allocated to social protection and targets including 4 million poor families, 18 million insured workers, and higher pensions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Government budget-and-target announcement with specific figures and program goals, directly tied to the 2022 fiscal plan.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sisi government through executive planning and budget-setting authority; implementation is shared with ministries and agencies.
contrary_evidence: This is a plan and budget target, not independent proof that all promised delivery was achieved.
The source is government-produced and may overstate intended benefits.

evidence.claim: The insurance authority said a 13% pension increase would take effect on April 1, 2022, benefiting 10.7 million citizens at a monthly cost of EGP 3.8 billion.
evidence.title: تنفيذا لتوجيهات السيد رئيس الجمهورية التأمينات "زيادة المعاشات بنسبة 13من اجمالى قيمة المعاش"
evidence.excerpt: The insurance authority said a 13% pension increase would take effect on April 1, 2022, benefiting 10.7 million citizens at a monthly cost of EGP 3.8 billion.
evidence.source_locator: search result snippet and article header/summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official social-insurance announcement with precise beneficiary counts and fiscal cost, but I could not cleanly extract the page text through the browser.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the president's directives and implemented through the social-insurance apparatus; the announcement is official but not independently audited here.
contrary_evidence: A pension boost helps purchasing power but does not by itself prove broad, durable welfare improvement.
Nominal increases can be eroded quickly by inflation.

evidence.claim: The article says there was a presidential directive to continue implementing universal health insurance despite global economic challenges, and to consider extending coverage to more people in need to strengthen social protection.
evidence.title: تكليف رئاسي باستكمال تطبيق التأمين الصحى الشامل رغم التحديات الاقتصادية العالمية
evidence.excerpt: The article says there was a presidential directive to continue implementing universal health insurance despite global economic challenges, and to consider extending coverage to more people in need to strengthen social protection.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government notice with a direct presidential directive and concrete policy direction, but the snippet is all I could retrieve cleanly.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sisi via a presidential directive; operational rollout still depends on health institutions.
contrary_evidence: The source shows intent and direction, not completed nationwide coverage in 2022.
The page is a government statement, so effect estimates need independent corroboration.

evidence.claim: The Decent Life Initiative, initiated experimentally in 2019 by President Abdel-Fattah El-Sisi, aimed to improve living standards, infrastructure, and basic services including healthcare across the countryside; the project covered 4,658 villages and 58 percent of Egypt’s population.
evidence.title: 1st stage of Decent Life initiative to conclude by December
evidence.excerpt: The Decent Life Initiative, initiated experimentally in 2019 by President Abdel-Fattah El-Sisi, aimed to improve living standards, infrastructure, and basic services including healthcare across the countryside; the project covered 4,658 villages and 58 percent of Egypt’s population.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official portal reproducing a contemporaneous report with specific scale and purpose; the underlying item is attributed to Al-Ahram Online.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High attribution: the initiative is explicitly presidential, though implementation is decentralized across ministries and governorates.
contrary_evidence: The article describes scope and goals more clearly than verified welfare outcomes.
The original schedule slipped because of global supply delays.

evidence.claim: The ministry reported EGP 321 billion in social subsidies, grants, and benefits in 2021/22, a target of EGP 356 billion in 2022/23, and said Egypt’s social-protection programs had helped reduce poverty and improve living standards, including in the poorest village clusters reached by Hayah Karima.
evidence.title: In observance of the International Day for the Eradication of Poverty, the Ministry of Planning and Economic Development issues a report on social protection and poverty reduction efforts
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Planning and Economic Development
evidence.excerpt: The ministry reported EGP 321 billion in social subsidies, grants, and benefits in 2021/22, a target of EGP 356 billion in 2022/23, and said Egypt’s social-protection programs had helped reduce poverty and improve living standards, including in the poorest village clusters reached by Hayah Karima.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific budgetary figures and named social programs from an official economic-planning report, though the poverty effects are self-reported.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 fiscal-year reporting with some lagged outcome claims.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to state policy under Sisi via government budgeting and program rollout; outcome claims are partly mediated by earlier baseline trends.
contrary_evidence: The report is self-evaluative and not independent.
Some poverty figures lag the target year and may not isolate 2022 effects.

evidence.claim: The Prime Minister said the government was expanding the social-protection umbrella by adding an extra one million families to Takaful and Karama, bringing beneficiaries to more than 20 million citizens, and that the program had already reached 4.6 million families.
evidence.title: PM follows up with social solidarity min. efforts to expand social protection programs
evidence.excerpt: The Prime Minister said the government was expanding the social-protection umbrella by adding an extra one million families to Takaful and Karama, bringing beneficiaries to more than 20 million citizens, and that the program had already reached 4.6 million families.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government summary with precise beneficiary totals, but retrieved as a snippet rather than a fully accessible page.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to presidential directives executed by the cabinet and social-solidarity ministry; implementation is institutional rather than personal.
contrary_evidence: Expansion demonstrates reach, not necessarily quality or neutrality.
Beneficiary growth does not by itself prove that coverage kept pace with inflation.

evidence.claim: The World Bank announced US$500 million to expand and strengthen Takaful and Karama; as of June 2022 the program covered 3.69 million households, about 12.84 million people, with 74 percent of cardholders/direct beneficiaries women and 67 percent of cash going to Upper Egypt.
evidence.title: New World Bank Financing Will Expand and Strengthen Egypt’s Flagship Social Protection Program
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank announced US$500 million to expand and strengthen Takaful and Karama; as of June 2022 the program covered 3.69 million households, about 12.84 million people, with 74 percent of cardholders/direct beneficiaries women and 67 percent of cash going to Upper Egypt.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank press release with specific coverage and distribution statistics, directly tied to a government program and the financing it received.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year 2022 program coverage and year-end financing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to state policy under Sisi, with implementation through the social-solidarity ministry and donor co-financing; not all outcomes are solely ruler-controlled.
contrary_evidence: External financing indicates the program required donor support, so it is not purely a domestic achievement.
Coverage data show reach but not benefit adequacy relative to inflation.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said Egypt was experiencing a spike in inflation and abrupt portfolio outflows, that real incomes would be adversely impacted, that poverty may increase because of inflation, and that budgeted education spending remained at 2.0 percent of GDP in FY2022/23, below FY2021/22.
evidence.title: Egypt Economic Monitor, December 2022: Strengthening Resilience through Fiscal and Education Sectors Reforms
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said Egypt was experiencing a spike in inflation and abrupt portfolio outflows, that real incomes would be adversely impacted, that poverty may increase because of inflation, and that budgeted education spending remained at 2.0 percent of GDP in FY2022/23, below FY2021/22.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: A detailed World Bank country monitor with clear line-level claims about inflation, poverty risk, and education spending.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to global shocks, but policy response under Sisi mattered through fiscal, monetary, and education choices.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes the government announced social mitigation packages and reforms.
Some negative effects are driven by external shocks rather than domestic policy alone.

evidence.claim: The IMF said Egypt’s package would preserve macroeconomic stability, restore buffers, reduce inflation, ensure debt sustainability, and increase social spending and social safety nets to protect the vulnerable while moving toward private-sector-led growth.
evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Approves 46-month US$3 billion Extended Arrangement for Egypt
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said Egypt’s package would preserve macroeconomic stability, restore buffers, reduce inflation, ensure debt sustainability, and increase social spending and social safety nets to protect the vulnerable while moving toward private-sector-led growth.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Clear IMF press release with explicit policy prescriptions and social-protection language.
evidence.period_fit: Late-2022 policy response to the target-year shock.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Sisi government’s policy choice to seek and accept IMF-supported adjustment, but the package is joint with external lenders and conditional on implementation.
contrary_evidence: This is a program design, not proof of delivered welfare gains in 2022.
Austerity-like elements can offset some protection gains if implementation is harsh.

evidence.claim: UNICEF said its teacher-preparedness package enabled safe school operations and back-to-learning support for refugee community schools, creating safe learning conditions for over 17,528 migrant and refugee children and supporting about 30,000 children to learn online and in person.
evidence.title: Learning against all odds
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF said its teacher-preparedness package enabled safe school operations and back-to-learning support for refugee community schools, creating safe learning conditions for over 17,528 migrant and refugee children and supporting about 30,000 children to learn online and in person.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UNICEF country story with specific beneficiary counts and clearly described interventions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable only in part to government cooperation; UNICEF and donors implemented much of the intervention, but it operated with state school access and consent.
contrary_evidence: The article is programmatic and does not measure national learning outcomes.
The need for this intervention itself shows existing disruption and vulnerability.

evidence.claim: UNICEF said a 2021-initiated program aimed to create an inclusive learning environment for refugee and migrant children in Egypt, and that over 3,534 students had benefited from a more inclusive and enabling environment with improved quality and relevance of education.
evidence.title: Learning as a driver for social cohesion
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF said a 2021-initiated program aimed to create an inclusive learning environment for refugee and migrant children in Egypt, and that over 3,534 students had benefited from a more inclusive and enabling environment with improved quality and relevance of education.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific UNICEF program description with beneficiary count and direct relevance to vulnerable-group education access.
evidence.period_fit: Program active in 2022, though launched in 2021.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to the Egyptian education system’s willingness to permit and host the program; the delivery itself is largely UNICEF/CARE driven.
contrary_evidence: The program serves a limited subset of children, not the whole system.
It is still a targeted intervention rather than a broad national reform outcome.

evidence.claim: UNHCR said Egypt reiterated its commitment to maintain and expand services for refugees and asylum-seekers in health and education, that refugee and asylum-seeker students with expired documents could still enroll in public schools, and that they were included in COVID response and vaccination plans on equal footing with Egyptians.
evidence.title: Thanks to Egypt, Thousands of Refugees are able to Access Health and Education Services
evidence.excerpt: UNHCR said Egypt reiterated its commitment to maintain and expand services for refugees and asylum-seekers in health and education, that refugee and asylum-seeker students with expired documents could still enroll in public schools, and that they were included in COVID response and vaccination plans on equal footing with Egyptians.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNHCR country office report with concrete policy details and explicit government commitment, though not a government source itself.
evidence.period_fit: Late-2021 baseline that carried into the 2022 period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to the Egyptian government’s cooperation and legal admissions policy; UNHCR and partners implemented and documented the access channels.
contrary_evidence: This does not prove nationwide service quality or equal treatment in every locality.
It shows access policy, not full outcome equality.

evidence.claim: UNHCR said its 2022 cross-sectional survey monitored access to and utilization of key health services among refugees living in Egypt in order to identify barriers encountered.
evidence.title: Health access and utilization survey among refugees in Egypt - 2022
evidence.excerpt: UNHCR said its 2022 cross-sectional survey monitored access to and utilization of key health services among refugees living in Egypt in order to identify barriers encountered.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official UNHCR documentation portal with clear description of the survey purpose and target population, though not the survey findings themselves.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is mainly a monitoring instrument; it supports attribution analysis by showing that refugee health access was being actively tracked, not merely presumed.
contrary_evidence: The page does not report findings, so it cannot by itself establish whether access improved.
It is stronger as evidence of measurement than of outcomes.

evidence.claim: UNICEF said the effects of climate change and environmental degradation hit children hardest, especially those living in poorer communities, because they are more exposed and have less capacity to respond.
evidence.title: Children's Climate Risk Index: Egypt Report
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF said the effects of climate change and environmental degradation hit children hardest, especially those living in poorer communities, because they are more exposed and have less capacity to respond.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF country report with a direct inequality claim, though it is framed as a general vulnerability assessment rather than a ruler-specific outcome study.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Contextual rather than directly attributable; it describes structural vulnerability that Sisi’s policies may mitigate or aggravate.
contrary_evidence: The report is about structural risk, not direct policy delivery.
It does not isolate 2022 government performance.

evidence.claim: The report says multidimensional poverty affected 21 percent of Egyptians in 2022, that poverty was much higher in rural than urban areas, and that services and employment were the biggest contributors to overall deprivation.
evidence.title: Multidimensional poverty in Egypt: an in-depth analysis
evidence.excerpt: The report says multidimensional poverty affected 21 percent of Egyptians in 2022, that poverty was much higher in rural than urban areas, and that services and employment were the biggest contributors to overall deprivation.
evidence.source_locator: highlight bullets in the report landing page
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Retrospective publication using 2022 data from an inter-agency report; the 2022 figures are clear even though the publication is later.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the 2022 social and economic environment under Sisi, but the report does not separate policy from inherited or global shocks.
contrary_evidence: This is retrospective and not a direct contemporaneous 2022 administrative record.
It measures deprivation, not the exact causal share of Sisi’s policy.

unresolved_gaps: No direct evidence of Sisi personally making a 2022 nuclear-safety, command-and-control, or crisis-escalation choice.
Concrete durable-conflict outcomes are thin beyond mediation and de-escalatory posture.
Exact chains of command and the effectiveness of pardon/reform mechanisms remain opaque.
There was no 2022 election, so contestability and transfer-rule evidence remains mostly structural rather than event-based.
Household-level distribution and implementation depth of the reform package are still thin.
Independent 2022 household outcome data are still thin, especially on whether transfers and pensions offset inflation.
There is no direct 2022 asset declaration, audit trail, procurement finding, or court judgment tying Sisi or close family to specific private gain from office.
Direct truthfulness/correction evidence from Sisi's own statements is still thin.
Direct evidence of Sisi's personal steering of tactical adjustments and durable outcome attribution remains limited.

run_provenance.source_mix_note: Rich source metadata and chapter-specific reviewer exclusions were preserved during deterministic conversion.
